name: X-linked Alport Syndrome

criteria.description: Positive family history of hematuria or renal failure consistent with X-linked inheritance
Persistent microscopic hematuria starting in childhood
Bilateral sensorineural hearing loss, typically developing in late childhood or adolescence
Anterior lenticonus or other characteristic ocular abnormalities
Electron microscopy showing irregular thickening and splitting of the glomerular basement membrane

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Persistent hematuria plus either family history consistent with X-linked inheritance or characteristic renal biopsy findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can confirm diagnosis but is not always required if clinical and biopsy criteria are met.

searchTerms: blood in urine visible only under microscope
tiny amounts of blood in urine

pathognomonic.symptomName: Electron microscopy showing glomerular basement membrane lamellation and splitting
searchTerms: lamellated kidney membrane seen on microscopy
high blood pressure from kidney problems
blood pressure increase due to kidney issues

common.symptomName: Ocular abnormalities including macular flecks and cataracts
searchTerms: eye problems with spots and cataracts

occasional.symptomName: End-stage renal disease by early adulthood
Fatigue related to chronic kidney disease
searchTerms: fatigue linked to chronic kidney failure
low energy due to kidney problems

rare.symptomName: Leiomyomatosis of esophagus or tracheobronchial tree
rare.notes: Rare association in some COL4A5 mutations
searchTerms: smooth muscle tumors in esophagus or airway
leiomyoma in esophagus or bronchial tubes

rare.symptomName: Cardiomyopathy secondary to chronic renal disease
searchTerms: heart muscle disease from kidney failure
cardiomyopathy due to chronic renal disease
heart problems secondary to kidney disease
nerve issues caused by kidney toxins

laboratory: Proteinuria detected by urine protein quantification
Elevated serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen in advanced disease
imaging: Renal ultrasound showing normal to small echogenic kidneys in late stages
Ocular slit-lamp examination revealing anterior lenticonus
other: Renal biopsy with electron microscopy showing characteristic basement membrane abnormalities

distinguishingFeatures: Mutations in COL4A3 or COL4A4 genes
Isolated microscopic hematuria without progression to renal failure
Thinning but not lamellation of glomerular basement membrane on biopsy

redFlags: Early onset persistent microscopic hematuria in male patient
Family history of renal failure or hearing loss consistent with X-linked inheritance
Development of sensorineural hearing loss in adolescence
references: Kashtan CE. Alport syndrome: Achieving clarity on the genetic and clinical spectrum. Kidney Int. 2021;99(3):566-568.
Savige J, et al. Alport syndrome. Clin J Am Soc Nephrol. 2015;10(4):703-715.
